utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Saxon, you're standing. Is there something before I have the witness affirm?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I had left a request last night with the court officer to see if I could simply raise a very brief matter before the witness begins his testimony. I can do it at another time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there a reason for the witness not to be in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The witness may be present in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me deal with the witness first. Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. Now, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Very briefly, Your Honour, the Prosecution may have caused some confusion with its most recent two-week list of witnesses because we realised today that the latest schedule referred to not this witness but the following witness, Mr. Nazim Bushi as a 92 bis witness. That is incorrect, Your Honour. Mr. Bushi will be a fully viva voce witness pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision of 30 March this year. The second issue is simply to inform the Chamber of a disclosure error that I discovered late last week. It's simply that the Prosecution located a hard copy printout of an article that had been taken from the Internet at the site of the Institute for War and Peace Reporting, IWPR and it was an article that had been written by a Prosecution witness, Peter Bouckaert. And the article discussed the situation in Macedonia in 2001 and also touched upon the events in Ljuboten. And in the Prosecution's submission, this is something that should have been disclosed earlier under Rule 66(A)(ii). So it was disclosed on Friday afternoon to the Defence. And I just wanted to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Ms. Motoike will be leading the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think Ms. Motoike has some questions for you now. Yes Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Sir, is your name Zoran Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you a citizen of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is your ethnicity Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in August of 2001 were you the chief of the personal security for the former minister, Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you recall when you were appointed to this particular position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: When the minister became minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. That would be sometime in the beginning of 2000 then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And for how long did you hold this particular position; that is, is the chief of the personal security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Until September 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you currently still a member of the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what position do you hold now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Police officer in police station Dracevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And how long have you been with the Macedonian police to date?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: 16 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. The security unit you were the chief of, was this unit part of the sector for security and protection?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Formally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in 2001, did you know a person by the name of Blagoja Jakovoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: My apologies. Can you please repeat the year?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And was Mr. Jakovoski, was he one of the persons under your supervision as chief?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Was the sector for security and protection a part of the Ministry of Interior in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As chief of this personal security unit, did you issue orders to your subordinates within this particular unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And was there a chain of command in the sector for security and protection, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: In part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain to us what you mean by "in part"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: The sector for security, Zivko Gacovski, assistant minister of the interior is the superior. In the line of things, he is the superior of the 6th unit which is in charge of security of VIP persons, the minister of the interior, prime minister, president, et cetera. However, direct orders regarding securities were mainly through the minister in person. Zivko Gacovski, that is to say the assistant minister took more care of the technical aspects of the work, the material aspects of the work.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand you, the minister would be the one mainly issuing orders, and then the assistant minister took care of more technical aspects?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I told you that the assistant minister of the 6th department is Zivko Gacovski, Gacovski. He in charge of the 6th department. However the security of the minister functioned in the way in which I just presented it to you. We received orders from the minister. Therefore, Zivko Gacovski, almost -- was almost never informed of our whereabouts and our movements. He took care more regarding issues of protocol for foreign delegations and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. In your position as chief of security, did you spend a lot of time in Mr. Boskoski's presence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As the chief of security, did you consider yourself a close associate of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Surely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you come to respect Mr. Boskoski as the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And when Mr. Boskoski was the minister, did he interact often with police officers and commanders within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And as the minister, do you recall if Mr. Boskoski was close to the police officers and the commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: He was very close with the police officers. Most often with the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: During the time he was minister did he often express concern for the police officers within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: For the police officers as well as for all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And as the minister, did Mr. Boskoski often ask the commanders about how the officers within their particular units were doing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know. I think on a regular basis, on each collegium, he informed himself about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As the minister in 2001, did Mr. Boskoski also try to keep abreast of what the officers were doing in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I presumed this would be so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. In 2001, did Mr. Boskoski visit the crisis areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not only the crisis but also other areas as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, in particular, let's just focus on the crisis areas. As chief of security did you accompany Mr. Boskoski at that time when he visited the crisis areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Most often, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in 2001, do you recall if Mr. Boskoski visited police units in Karadak and Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: During these visits did you often go to places at the time -- at the same time these events were unfolding at these particular areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not understand you well. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise; it was my phrasing. My question was when you went to the crisis areas, are there occasions when you would go to a particular area and -- and the events at that area were unfolding at that time. That is, everything was still happening at that time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So when you visited the crisis areas then, did you meet with, or did Mr. Boskoski meet with the units in those areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: With the commanding personnel with officers, yes, to inform himself of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time would he also - he, being Mr. Boskoski - would he also give orders to the commanders of these units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Never in my presence. Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But you saw Mr. Boskoski meeting with the commanders, you said, of the police units in these areas.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I told you this. His presence was there to get firsthand about the situation on the given ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In June and/or July of 2001, do you recall visiting other places with the minister? And I know that you spoke of not only crisis areas but other areas. Do you recall visiting areas such as Zilce, Tetovo and Ratae about the security situations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Sir, if we could, I would like to, with the assistance of Ms. Walpita, show a video-clip at this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It is 65 ter 974. And, for the record, this is a clip from Macedonian Television. It was made around July and/or August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, you said you were a police officer for 16 years. I would like you to take a look at the screen. Could you tell us whether you recognise the vehicles that are depicted in this particular video?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are these vehicles what one would term as an APC and/or Hermelin vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Hermelin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are these vehicles like the Hermelins that were used by the Ministry of Interior back in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of Interior, though, have what are vehicles like this that are called Hermelin, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Hermelin yes; but without the machine-gun [indiscernible] dome.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. So actually, let's show another part of this particular clip, please. So we can continue to play. For the record that clip was at 9.08 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you reference a machine-gun -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like our colleague -- would like to ask our colleagues to make the time more precise of these clips, because it is -- was mentioned very broadly in July/August of that year, but on this clip we do not see the year that was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to assist, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we received this clip from the Macedonian -- it is a clip from the Macedonian Television, and at that time we were given an approximate date of this because of the area in which we believe that these -- this footage was shot would be July to August of 2001. And I apologise I can't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, we're now looking at another part of this particular clip. And you had mentioned earlier a machine-gun. Do you see the machine gun here that is basically mounted on the top of what looks to be a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see a machine-gun which is fixated with some sort of improvised apparatus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in 2001 are you saying that did you not see vehicles like this, as far as in the Ministry of Interior, with the machine-gun strapped on like that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Until 2002, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And that particular footage is at 15.06 of this particular clip. If we continue to play. Actually, that is the end of it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours I would at this time be seeking to tender this particular video-clip which is at 1.26.06 to 1.26.18, part of 65 ter 974.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, prior to your decision we wanted to object because the Prosecution itself does not know the time of this clip. Furthermore, the witness could not recognise this Hermelin at the time, which is offered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not my understanding of his evidence. I thought he recognised the vehicle but indicated that it is wasn't fitted with a machine-gun in the way that was shown on that photograph until 2002. Is that not the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what we heard, that this was the testimony of the witness. However, the Prosecution offered this as evidence for July and August of 2001. However, as a whole, the statement has -- is also included in the statement of the witness, so with the explanation which you have given us, we accept this as such. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me make it clear: The Prosecution has not been able to lead from this witness the date upon which that video film was taken. The witness says that he recognised this photograph-- or this film to be of Hermelin vehicles, of a type that was in use in 2001 but he does not recognise the machine-guns fitted as they were in the photograph. He saw that not before 2002. Now, on that basis, do you want to tender this video, Ms. Motoike?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P453, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Trajkovski, again, we'd like to show you a different clip from the same 65 ter number, 974.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And for the record this is it again the same Macedonian Television clip that we received that we believe was sought sometime in July and August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, you earlier testified that Mr. Boskoski and you would visit the areas regarding security situations and you've seen this particular clip. We've stopped it here now, and there are some people depicted on the video-clip that is here on the screen. Do you recognise whose's depicted here in the video?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I recognise the minister of interior, my colleague Blagoja, and the commander of the police station, an ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you know where this particular police station was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe this is the border crossing of Jezince.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in this particular -- you said that your colleague Blagoja. Is that Blagoja Jakovoski we've discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I can assist the record is that the person that is, as you look at the screen, on the left of the photo wearing the sun-glasses and the baseball cap?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you've indicated you recognise Mr. Boskoski. That would be the person, then, in the middle of the screen who is wearing the sun-glasses and the belt. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So the police commander that you've also testified about, is that the person that is wearing a blue vest in the right of the photo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were you -- during this visit, were you present as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And can you tell us around what time this visit occurred, what month and year?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I only know that during the visit there were international presence there, OSCE, UNPROFOR or UNPREDEP. I don't recall how it was called at that time exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And so for the record, we stopped this at 31.06 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we can continue to play, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could stop it for a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski what we're seeing now through this video is basically some cars and some what you've described as Hermelins travelling down a road. Do you recall if when you went to visit places with Mr. Boskoski, is this basically what -- what kind of vehicles you would travel in?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall ever travelling with the minister in this kind of a what I'd loose term convoy or series of cars?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: As I am able to recall, only to one other place.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And what place would that have been to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Police station Matejce. However, this wasn't a convoy but there was a Hermelin there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we can continue to play, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this we have stopped at 1 minute 3 seconds, .4 on the clip. Again, Mr. Trajkovski, do you recognise the persons depicted in this particular clip?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who you recognise? And if you could, describe where they are in the picture.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I recognise myself, the last one with the black cap on this photograph, on this clip, Mr. Risto Galevski in the middle, and in front the minister of the interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I'm sorry. I'm going to ask you if you remember when this particular visit occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall if this visit was around the same time as the prior clip that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I presume, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us what location are you visiting at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe border crossing Jezince.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: When you spoke of visits by Mr. Boskoski to areas regarding the security situations, would this video and the other video be an example of those visits?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What was the purpose in visiting this -- these particular areas, these two borders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: When these visits occurred, did Mr. Boskoski do the same thing you've described earlier, and that is meet with the police officers there at those particular locations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question? I did not understand you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. When these two particular visits you said you were -- you were at these visits, the two clips that we've seen. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not -- I don't see two visits here. This is one visit in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. I guess I'm referring to the other clip that we saw where Mr. Boskoski and your colleague Mr. Jakovoski were there. Do you remember that clip?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Was that a separate, a different location than is depicted in this particular clip?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think not. I think this is the same place in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. My apologies. And if this is the same place in question, I'm just asking you if this -- these two clips that we've seen, is that an example of the visits that Mr. Boskoski would make to units in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Surely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. During this particular visit, did Mr. Boskoski meet with any of the police officers? You said that was a commander there in the other clip. Did he meet with police officers there at this particular location?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot recall precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Continue to play, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. You can stop. Your Honours, I would also seek to tender this particular clip. For the record the time from the 65 ter 974 clip is 1 hour 26 minutes 6 seconds to 1 hour 27 minutes 8 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P454, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, this visit that we've just seen in the video-clip, that was covered by the media. Were there occasions when the minister visited areas and the media were not present?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't remember. There must have been events where media were not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Going back to the visits that you recalled at places like Zilce and Tetovo, do you recall if the minister gave orders to the police commanders who were present at those locations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I will repeat them as did I at the beginning. The minister of the interior never issued such order in my presence. He was just a representative of the government in the Ministry of Interior. He was a political figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. I guess my question was -- okay, I withdraw that. During your visits to places like Zilce and Tetovo, would the minister speak to the commanders as well as the civilians who were present?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: To be honest, I can't remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall making a -- providing a witness statement to the Office of the Prosecution on 27 April 2004?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I recall very little. I signed that statement then in the English language. It was read to me, and to this date, I haven't read it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I guess my question is: Then you recall making a statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And would reviewing a part of that statement which pertains to the subject matter we're on, would reviewing a part of that statement refresh your recollection as to the question I asked you about meetings with the commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me then look at the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: We have hard copies, if the usher could assist us, please. This is also uploaded in e-court, ERN range is N000-6835 to N000-6844. And the Macedonian version has MF on the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could, Mr. Trajkovski, ask to you look at -- first of all you indicated that you did sign the witness statement. Do you see that, your signature there on the front of the statement as well as the last page and every page of the statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the bottom left corner everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention in particular to paragraph 22?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And we could pull that up on the screen as well for you in the Macedonian version. It is it on page 6 of the English and page 6 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the first part of this sentence says: "Other activities of the minister in reference to the security situation in the time-period of June and/or July were that we were visiting Zilce, Tetovo and Ratae. By these occasion the minister had conversations with the civilians and local representatives and was giving orders to the police commanders." Do you see that, Mr. Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And after reading that, are you able to tell us now whether or not you remember if the minister spoke to the commanders as well as the civilians at these particular locations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I remember that there were moments when he spoke to them, but he told me that that was just an interview with certain superior officer and never an order. So what is written here, I haven't said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. But had you an opportunity, though, back in 2004 though you said to read the statement -- have the statement read to you in English, is that right -- I mean read to you in Macedonian. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: The only thing I signed was the statement in the English language, a language that I have only passive command of. The statement was read to me by a gentleman, I think it was Thomas Kuehnel, and I signed every page of it. This is the first time I see the statement in the Macedonian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So we're clear, you said it was read to you by a gentleman named Thomas Kuehnel. Was it read to you by him in English and then it was interpreted at the same time into Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And going back to these particular visits of Zilce, Tetovo and Ratae, if there were complaints about the behaviour of the police, do you recall how the minister handled those?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: So specifically about this territory, Zilce, Ratae, Tetovo villages, I don't remember that there have ever been complaints by the commanding officers regarding any problems with the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In other areas, if there were complaints, meaning other areas, meaning other sites or crisis areas that you visited if there were complaints about the behaviour of certain officers do you recall how the minister would handle those?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me just go back to the statement -- the sentence I said before. In item 23, what I wrote there is that the reason why he was so frequently travelling personally to the crisis area was to get firsthand information. So not to issue orders but to get information. So this is related to your previous question. But to the question that you ask now, yes, I remember the Vaksince case when the commander of the Tigers unit, upon a complaint of one of the superior officers, I suppose it would have been an army general in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, Toni Mandarovski was suspend from duty and then there was a disciplinary action against him and after that he was replaced from the office.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Since we're on the topic of the Tigers, in 2001, then, do you know of a unit called the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And you said that -- well, let me just ask you this: Minister Boskoski then responded to this complaint by the army official regarding the commander of the Tigers at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What kind of contact did Mr. Boskoski, outside of this particular issue with Commander Mandarovski, what kind of contact did Minister Boskoski in 2001 have with the unit called the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have seen Mr. Toni Mandarovski several time in the Ministry of the Interior always at the collegium that the minister of the interior convened with the commanders of the other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And going back then -- well, let me ask you this: How often did this collegium meet with the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think that most commonly it was once a week.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And who were the other persons who were present at this collegium?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: This collegium or any collegium?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: This particular collegium, the one that you're saying met once a week who had at least Commander Mandarovski and Mr. Boskoski present.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: It seems that you are trying to twist my words. I said that I had seen Mr. Mandarovski at the Ministry of Interior whenever he would be invited to a collegium. But he was never alone with the minister. It does not mean that at every collegium he was necessarily present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise, I misunderstood you. Before we go on to this other topic then I'd like to ask you: My question to you before was discipline issues with officers and how Mr. Boskoski would handle those. Did you ever see any other disciplinary issues that were raised by persons and brought to Mr. Boskoski's attention in 2001, besides the incident in Vaksince.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you recall that if complaints about the behaviour of certain police officers were expressed, can you recall how the minister would handle those?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Except this case with Toni Mandarovski I don't recall any other but you know what is the procedure and it was followed, the disciplinary action.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we can go back to your statement, would reviewing your statement once again refresh your recollection as to this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could display the statement once again, please. It is the same page, same paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, you have it in the Macedonian language and the hard copy in front of you. If I could draw your attention to paragraph 22. And this is the last sentence of that particular paragraph. It is on page 6 of the statement. Let me just read it. It says: "For example, if the complaints about the behaviour of certain police officers were expressed, the minister took personal care about this, he was ex officio in charge of the police." Do you see this Mr. Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course I see it. The point of this sentence of mine is political responsibility. Political responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what exactly do you mean by "political responsibility"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: What happens with the police officers in the Ministry of Interior is a matter of a procedure. For instance, any improper conduct would lead to a procedure, to a disciplinary action. Political responsibility, if I read this now, the moment comes, I remember the protest in Skopje when part of the reserve forces were in front of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, and the minister requested that the prime minister in the government resigns because of the events, because of his political responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So you're saying that by this -- you recall making this statement with respect to the minister and him taking personal care about these issues. You recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But my question to you was, then, and I know you might have answered this but I just seek a clarification. My question was to you then if the minister had complaints about the behaviour of certain police officers, then what you're telling us is that he would follow some sort of procedure with respect to those complaints. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes, as far as I'm able to understand you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And to your knowledge, did Mr. Boskoski at the time when he was minister, ever propose or start a disciplinary action against any police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As chief of security, do you recall if Mr. Boskoski had a routine weekly schedule?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. By "no," I take it you mean you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Would looking at your statement again refresh your recollection as to this particular fact? Since you're looking at your statement, I will refer to you paragraph 20, which is on page 5 of the statement. It is page 5 of the English as well as page 5 of the Macedonian. And since you have the hard copy in front of you, Mr. Trajkovski, the bottom part of this particular paragraph starts with the words: "Normally at around 8 to 900 hours we arrived in the office every day of the week. The first thing he was reading his email -- his mail. At the same time he gave the order to the secretary (first name Violeta) of his office to call the police generals. Normally these police commanders were General Jovanovski, the head of the posebna unit; Vasko, last name unknown, the general of the Tigers; Goran Zdravkovski, the commander of the Lions; Goran Stojkov, and it goes on to the next page. Police general Risto Galevski and maybe some other deputies and occasionally the directors of the public security Goran Mitevski, and the UBK Director, Nikola Spasovski. Also some other commanders depending on the current events. These meetings happened normally four to five times per week on regular basis." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And after reviewing that, do you now recall whether Mr. Boskoski had a routine weekly schedule?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm reading the statement and I think that a mistake had been made here, or several mistakes. Namely it is not possible that during that period at the same time both Risto Galevski and Zoran Jovanovski were police generals, since the General Jovanovski was after General Risto Galevski. So in this statement, or this part of the statements, I don't recall precisely, or it might have been translated incorrectly or there is a misunderstanding. And, secondly, since I said once a week was the usual frequency of the collegiums and when I think -- four or five times I think I was referring to the monthly basis and not weekly basis as it is written here at the end of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So then are you telling us that he did have a routine per week and that meetings with these particular persons albeit not all of them, maybe, did occur on a weekly basis?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And just following up on what you had commented on about Commander Mandarovski, you said that at times he was invited to the collegium. The collegium you were referring to that he was invited to, would that have been these meetings, these weekly meetings that the minister had?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: You are drawing me into questions -- you are asking me to answer questions that were outside of my competence. I never now whom he needed to invite to a collegium or whom he needed to meet. My duties were related to the security, safety of the minister of the interior and nothing more than that. I'm telling I recall that several times at a collegium I have seen Toni Mandarovski present, which does not mean that I needed to be at the building of the Ministry of the Interior at all times so that I see who is coming and who is going.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay, So at times then, if I understand you correctly, at times then Commander Mandarovski would attend these meetings with these other generals and the Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, at times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall knowing a person in 2001 named Zoran Jovanovski who was also known as Bucuk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I know him since around 1986/1987.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in 2001, do you recall ever seeing the former Minister Boskoski meet with Mr. Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't remember that the minister of the interior met Zoran Jovanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall if they ever had any -- do you recall ever seeing Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Jovanovski at the same restaurants? Might not have been a planned meeting, but do you ever recall seeing that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Of course it was not a planned meeting, and of course I remember that there were certain places that we frequented, and Mr. Zoran Jovanovski was there also, not often.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In 2001, I know we've spoken about the Tiger unit, but do you recall the formation of a special unit in the MOI, the Ministry of Interior, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you mean another special unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: In 2001, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you aware of a special unit called the Lions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall a training exercise that took place at a location called Penus?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Penus, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall when this particular training exercise took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely. I know that it was very cold. I think it was towards the end of the year, 2001, or at the most, beginning of 2002. But I think it was the end of 2001, somewhere November.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you remember if the Lions participated in this particular training exercise?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't recall. There were many uniformed police officers. I can't recall. I don't think that they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. You said that you don't recall. Would looking at your statement refresh your recollection as to this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And would looking at that refresh your recollection? I'll draw your attention to paragraph 21 of the Macedonian, it is page 6, the English is page 6. In that particular paragraph it says: "In the training area Penus near Stipe mainly used by the police, the minister visited a military presentational exercise of the police. It may be said that also the Rapid Intervention Unit Lions also participated in that exercise. According to my opinion, this was in the summertime before the events of Ljuboten. Being asked, I said that I am very sure about the Lions' participation in the Penus exercise." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: But this expression "very sure" is not known to me. I never say that I'm very sure. I'm either sure or I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at the time then in 2004 when you made this statement you indicated that you were very sure about the Lions' participation in the Penus exercise. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is written here that I'm very sure, but I have said I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Were you with the Minister Boskoski during the weekend of 10 and 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, my name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I am defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I proceed with asking you some questions, I would like to ask you to hear out a -- my appeal. I presume that you understand the language in which I'm speaking to you, and I -- I understand the language which you speak. However, my questions and your responses need to be translated so that the Honourable Court and members in the courtroom can understand what I'm asking you and what you're responding to me. Therefore, I would ask you to wait for the question to be interpreted and only then to proceed with your response to the question. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Trajkovski, that as of 1992 you are employed in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that, you had finished secondary education, and for a time you worked other jobs, and then as of 1992, you were permanently employed in the Ministry of Interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After being employed in 1992, first, you were inspector in the police station Gostivar, up until July 1997. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, police officer in the police station Gostivar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this job in the police station Gostivar you worked in the unit for securing diplomatic and consular offices. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As of 1999, you worked in the sector for operative surveillance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of my learned colleague you said that you were the head of the personal security of Minister Boskoski. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this regards, I would ask you to help me clarify one response which was not sufficiently clarified. To the previous question of my learned colleague, you said that you became the head of the security at the time when Ljube Boskoski became minister. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of my colleague on page 3, line 16, when she -- it was suggested to you that this was at the beginning of 2002, at the year 2000, you responded affirmative, you said yes. My question, it may be a mistake, if I were to say to that you Minister Boskoski became minister in May 2001, would this recall -- would remind you that you became head of his personal security in the May of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, May 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that after having been appointed head of the personal security of the minister, is it correct that you were directly included in the election of the team of the personal security of the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct then when members of the security teams are selected that the head of security conducts consultations with the person that is being secured, that is to say that you had consultations on this matter with Minister Boskoski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Minister Boskoski requested of you only that this team include persons that will carry out their jobs professionally?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you concur with me that the minister was not burdened by the party affiliation of the team members or by other issues other than their professional attitude towards their job?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you became the head of the personal security you were a member of the VMRO party, but most of the persons in your team did not belong to any party. Some of them were even members of the opposition party. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I would ask you to please repeat your question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you became the head of the security of the minister, you were either a member of VMRO or you were a sympathizer of the VRMO. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, most of the team members which you selected on a professional basis were not members of the VMRO party, some did not belong to any party while others even belonged or were members of the opposition party, SDS, for example?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the security team of the minister came from the security team of the former President Gligorov. I had a colleague who is now working in the team of current President Crvenkovski. Another colleague worked with the previous minister of interior and it was said that he was a member of the SDS, a party which is now in the opposition and was in the opposition at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the minister did not raise any kind of issue of political affiliation of his personal security team at any which time, rather, let you, on professional basis, to make the selection of the team that can respond to the task. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you selected the team members of the security team from among a number of candidates, and following the suggestion of the minister to choose and to pick the best professionals. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of my learned colleague, you said that your security team as well as the other six teams that secured important persons in the Republic of Macedonia were in the sector of the security of the Ministry of Interior and in this regard, in view of the fact that you said formally, I would now ask you a number of questions in this regard. Do you recall having given this response to my learned colleague when asked this question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do remember saying formally because this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the sector for security in the Ministry of Interior which dealt with securing persons, was this in the -- was this in effect the so-called 6th department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, the 6th department.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the head of the 6th department was Mr. Zivko Gacovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Zivko Gacovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In responding to the question of my learned colleague, you said that the assistant minister dealt mainly with various issues of security, materiel, other resources. Am I correct in understanding this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I were to put it to you my understanding of the role of the assistant minister, regarding -- in regards to your -- to you but also other security teams, it would be in fact a role of the body which decided and dealt with issues of logistics, of security, that is to say, wages, finances, vehicles, equipment, would this understanding be the right understanding of the role of the security, this part of the security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Trajkovski, is it correct that -- that the other teams of personal security also included, for the most part, members, persons employed in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, with exception -- with the exception of the security team of the late President Trajkovski, the team of which also included people from another unit, which is not part of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thus, the security of the -- of president -- of Trajkovski in addition to teams from the Ministry of Interior included also members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, the special units Wolves. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Volci, yes, wolves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will go back to this question later on. But if I understood you correctly when you responded to the question of my colleague from the Prosecution, you said that you issued orders or tasks to your members of the team. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you also said that the tasks of security were determined together with the Minister Boskoski, depending on his daily or other obligations which he had. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that your colleagues also the heads of the permanent security of other important persons in the Republic of Macedonia also, in accordance to the duties they carried out, that they also issued orders to the members of the personal security of the person which is being secured. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct if I were to conclude that these important person which is being secured was the real boss, the real head of the security and that person in fact determined which jobs and tasks you should be carrying out. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your security team, you already said that Blagoja Jakovoski was part of it. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you recognised him on one of the video-clip that was shown to you. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your deputy of the team of the personal security of the minister was Branko Pejcinovski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Branko Pejcinovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition, the team -- the personal security team of Minister Boskoski also included Laste Mitkovski, Marijan Medarov, and Goran Jakimovski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Marijan Medarov and Goran Jakimovski were not entered into the transcript. Is it correct that you and other heads of security teams of Minister Boskoski, up until the fall of 2002, when VMRO became the opposition and other parties assumed power in the Republic of Macedonia. You were head of the security team until that time. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, the time during which you were head of the personal security of Minister Boskoski, would you be able to concur with me that this was a very difficult time for the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In particular, 2001 was a very difficult year, because in this period of time there was larger disturbances of the public order and peace and the state was exposed to terrorist attacks of the NLA also. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you testify to the fact that the police that in addition to regular duties during this period of time, also took part in the fights in crisis areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time then, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now until quarter past 4.00, although because of another matter, the Chamber may be a little delayed in returning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to all, and especially you, Ms. Residovic, that other matter took longer than expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, we spoke before the break that that was a difficult year for the police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that the public law and order were greatly disturbed that year.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the NLA, the terrorist groups, attacked the police stations and patrols.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you became the head of the personal security of the Minister Boskoski, you were aware that the Minister Boskoski, before working in the Ministry of Interior was not a professional police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also aware that the Minister Boskoski has lived for many years and worked in the Republic of Croatia and he had a completely different occupation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, most of his career he has spent in the health care. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said that you were close to the Minister Boskoski as head of his personal security, you could observe that the minister is very respectful of his professional line of command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He respected the opinions of his generals, and, actually, he never interfered with the line of command, and, as you said, he never issued an order in your presence, an order in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you also stated that he wanted to have firsthand information and that when he was appointed minister, he wanted to learn what the situation in the Ministry of Interior was, and what were the problems that the police officers in the field encounter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And was that willingness of his and the practice of his to learn about the problems firsthand the reason that you answered the question of my colleague Prosecutor that he did not go only to the crisis regions but he also made rounds of other areas of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, you stated that he went there just to get information about the situation and the problems because he believed that the -- it -- the political responsibility and the situation about the ministry was his. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when he would go to these departments or sectors of the Ministry of Interior and the police stations, could you also confirm that never in your presence he issued any order to those officers, heads of the departments or assistants?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I already stated this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he -- the minister never issued an order to the assistants or any other officers in the departments.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he never issued orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague asked you about his daily activities, and you explained that the minister would normally have a weekly meeting of the collegium members. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were then shown part of your statement that you gave to the Prosecutor's investigator in 2004, the paragraph 20, which enumerated the persons who could possibly be in attendance at the meetings. Do you recall that as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you immediately noticed that there was some misunderstanding; you said that it was written here that the General Jovanovski could not have been general at the same time that Risto Galevski was because he became a general and head, under-secretary of the police only after Risto Galevski left that office. Do you remember explaining that immediately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that sometimes also Toni Mandarovski came to the collegium meetings. He was, for a certain period of time, commander of the Tigers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since you also replied to one of the questions of the Prosecutor, in saying that Toni Mandarovski was suspended from duty because he refused to obey an order by a superior officer, do you remember that Toni Mandarovski came to some of those meetings before he was suspended from duty and that, after that, surely he was not invited and he would not attend. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Goran Zdravkovski was appointed commander of the Tigers in his place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in paragraph 20, there would be another misunderstanding here, because it would not have been possible for both Toni Mandarovski and Goran Zdravkovski to be in the same collegium in attendance because Goran Zdravkovski only came to this office when Toni Mandarovski was dismissed from this office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in this paragraph there is nothing about the time in relation to which you mentioned certain individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I remember only that I answered questions about collegiums and who were the persons who would be present in them most frequently and I just enumerated them without specifying the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I were to tell you also that Nikola Spasovski became director of the UBK only at the beginning of 2002 and that before that, Varucevski [phoen] was the director, then this would again corroborate that there is some confusion in this paragraph, because Nikola Spasovski could not have been in attendance at a collegium before 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also asked about the special unit Lions and you stated that you didn't know whether it had been established at all in 2001 or whether it happened towards the end of 2001. So if you mentioned that the Lions commander Goran Stojkov was in attendance at these meetings, that could only held through about the time after the establishment of the Lions, so towards the end of 2001 or in 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this, I would like to ask to you clarify one more thing. My learned colleague asked you about the participation in a drill. It is in page 27 [as interpreted], paragraph 2, a participation in an activity that took place at Penus. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what page it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Page 25, line 17, and my learned friend the Prosecutor asked you during this evidence of yours whether you were aware about the activity at Penus. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you immediately responded in saying that that was when it was very cold towards the end of 2001 or at the beginning of 2002, and you stated it could have been November. Do you remember giving this reply?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, my learned friend showed you again your statement, that is paragraph 21, which speaks about the military presentational exercise of the police at Penus. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were shown that you had stated then that you were certain, sure, that the exercise took place at Penus, but in that statement you had stated that this was during the summer. I will ask you now to look together -- to see a video-clip that is P277.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this area around Penus, the area you see in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you saw that it was quite cold, based on what the persons are wearing, because you can't see anything else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw this video-clip, Mr. Trajkovski, could you now say with certainty that it was really towards the end of 2001 or, as you stated, most probably in November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I am certain that it was towards the end of 2001, in November.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My learned colleague also asked you whether it was correct that the Minister Boskoski was close with his police officers and that he respected or appreciated their problems, something in that sense. Do you remember? I don't -- I can't quote precisely but that was the direction of the questions of my learned colleague. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Minister Boskoski really took interest in the problems in the Ministry of Interior and the deficiencies of the ministry which prevented the police as a whole to perform its duties with responsibility. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the time when Minister Boskoski became the minister of the interior, there were very many problems in the ministry that piled up for years and the minister attempted to resolve them, regardless of the fact that it was a crisis period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that in the meetings where he would visit the departments and the sectors of the Ministry of the Interior, he always asked that the problems are discussed only so that he, in his capacity of a minister, could undertake some activities, measures within the government or within the parliament to improve the situation of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that this was a time of crisis where the police officers were under great risks, also their life was under risk, could you say that the minister was a person who took humane care about the safety and the life of the police officers but, at the same time, he told them that they needed to act in accordance with the dignity of a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions of my learned colleague the Prosecutor you stated that he went to the crisis regions. If I say to that you the minister going to the areas where the police officers were exposed to the greatest risk wanted to give them morale support in the performance of such difficult tasks, then this would be the real reason why he went often to the areas where the police officers participated in the fights?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of his great care about the safety of the police officers, he was perceived as an unusual minister, because he sympathized with the problems of people more than the other ministers used to do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, he was known as someone who would meet people in the street and talk to them, and he never refused to have a word with people about their everyday life and problems. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And I would also add that if wealth would be measured by the number of friends, then certainly he is the richest person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But this closeness to people, regardless of where he would meet them, for you as his security, created new additional and big problems, because there were not many of you in his security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And particularly since unknown persons or strangers would come to him at the street, in a restaurant and he would shake hands with them regardless of the fact that he was not acquainted with them and that he had never met them before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, most often it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you as his body-guards needed often to be barrier between him and the people who wanted to shake hands with them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it happen sometimes that in public spaces, in a restaurant or in a street, you need to try to use your bodies as a shield, to prevent the people from coming to the minister and shaking hands with him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I say that the minister, apart from this closeness that he felt with the common people, was also a very sensitive person and he found very difficult to cope with every injury or killing of a subordinate person or just any person, you as his close associate can confirm that it was like this.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He would go and visit the wounded police officers in the hospital or at their homes, and he sent the -- the families of the killed police officers to his house in Istria, Croatia, so that they recover from the trauma they experienced with the loss of a family member and he did he it at his own expense. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you stated you never heard him issuing any order that treatment of his towards the ordinary police officers or towards the common people was not leading to him issuing orders to his subordinate officers or to the other employees, but he instead respected their rights and responsibilities at the places that -- where he visited?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague also asked you whether, in those encounters of Minister Boskoski with Zoran Jovanovski -- that is page 25, line 17, the of Prosecutor asked: "In 2001, did you see the Minister Boskoski meeting with Zoran Jovanovski?" You stated: "I don't remember that the minister met with Zoran Jovanovski." Then you were asked the following question: "Do you recall whether you ever saw them in the same restaurants, maybe that was not a planned meeting. Do you recall having seen that?" And you answered: "Of course that was not a planned meeting and of course that I remember that there were some places that we frequented and Zoran Jovanovski was there, not often." With regards to this exchange with my colleague the Prosecutor I'm asking you whether Minister Boskoski knew whether he was acquainted with Zoran Jovanovski with a nickname Bucuk. Are you aware of this at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can state that he does not know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that of course there were restaurants that you frequented and that Zoran Jovanovski would happen to be there, is it correct that Zoran Jovanovski, although he was at the same restaurant, he never sat with the Minister Boskoski or never talked to him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: He never sat with him and he never talked with him, with the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that as early as from 1986 you were acquainted with Zoran Jovanovski. Does that mean that you could have seen Zoran Jovanovski in that restaurant and note that he was seen or that the Minister Boskoski sat with him in a formal or an informal meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Of course one of my duties was to see the places that were visited and try to see who is there. Is something wrong with the interpretation? I'm hearing something.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I think we've heard your answer. Thank you. I wanted to clarify this question in view of the fact that after the exchange of the questions and answers, it remained unclear; you can state with certainty that you know Zoran Jovanovski, but that in your deep understanding of that time, the minister had never been with Zoran Jovanovski nor are you aware of the fact that he knows Zoran Jovanovski. Is this what you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I would ask you to repeat the question because there was an inadequate translation or something else. Therefore, I would ask to you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the response which you gave me at the moment, my question is: Have I understood correctly if I were to say that you knew Zoran Jovanovski, that you sometimes saw him in public restaurants where the minister was also present, where Minister Boskoski was also present, but that you do not know that Minister Boskoski knows Zoran Jovanovski nor have you at any given time seen him in the company of Zoran Jovanovski. Have I then understood correctly your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.
