utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My learned colleague also asked you about certain objections which -- which the minister had heard in visits in various areas about the demeanour of his police officers and the manners in which -- the reactions of the minister at that time. You listed a concrete example of Toni Mandarovski, who was suspended, after which a regular disciplinary procedure was led against Toni Mandarovski. Is this correct? After this, the Prosecutor asked you when the minister would hear of such objections, complaints, would he then send or follow a certain kind of procedure, disciplinary procedure? Your response was the following: "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] Well, yes, as far as I'm able to understand you, yes." [Interpretation] This would be the part of the statement. Do you recall having said this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to clarify this part of your response. In fact, you said, if I understood well your question, I'm now interested if, in the case of certain complaints about the demeanour of certain police officers, is this what you have said about certain procedures having been followed in the way, in the sense that you understood them? Would this mean that the minister respected the written procedure for establishing disciplinary responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This could not be understood in the context that the minister took part himself or looked into the procedure and how it was led, but that, rather, this was done by the responsible bodies in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this was done by the responsible bodies in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In regards to the disciplinary procedure, which my colleague from the Prosecution asked you about, do you know whether some police officers or policemen were punished, disciplinary punished and you responded that you did not know this, or that you do not recall of this. My question is: Is it correct that the ministry has information, reports, which show the number of disciplinary procedures each year or infringements of professional standards and how they were finalised, how they were closed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if the aim is to establish whether certain policemen and the manner in which the procedure was led in the disciplinary procedure and how they were punished, that this would be found in the information about the application of professional standards and disciplinary procedures. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is -- this can certainly be found there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back a little bit again to the -- the way the team security -- the security teams of important persons in Macedonia operated. You already mentioned that they were formally part of the Ministry of Interior with the exception of the part of the security team of the president of the Republic, and you explained how you selected the security team of Minister Boskoski. Is it correct that the security -- that the prime minister also had security as well as the president of the assembly, the minister of defence and some other important persons. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that all of these security teams acted independently of the Ministry of Interior and they planned their activities and they carried them out on the basis of the order or on the basis of the consultations with the person that was being secured or looked after?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is to say, they worked in the same way as you did in consultation with the Minister Boskoski's in carrying out the duties in protecting an individual.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither you nor your colleagues from other security did not, about these matters of security, consult Zivko Gacovski, the assistant minister for security nor did you submit any kind of reports to him. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be accurate if I were to conclude that the true control over the security was the person that was being protected, that is to say, the important person, be this the president, the prime minister or the minister. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Without exception, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that only your security, the personal security of the minister, was accommodated in the building of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The security of the president of the Republic was located in the building of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The security of the prime minister was located in -- in the building -- government building. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The security of the president of the assembly was in the building of the assembly. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Other ministries -- as for other ministries, in the buildings where these ministries were located. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the buildings of the respective ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you could concur with me if I were to say that your colleagues, the heads of the securities of other important persons, were in practice -- acted in practice independently from the Ministry of Interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never saw nor heard Minister Boskoski giving any kind of order to another head of security or to a body-guard of another person with the exception of you, as his own security.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Only to me and our own security team.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you never saw the minister in the company of any other members of the security of any other person which was protected in accordance with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It could happen that perhaps on a meeting a number of such persons were present and together with them, a large number of the security, that the minister just as everybody else could -- could extend his greetings to you as members of the security, just as the president and the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. During such meetings when there were Security Council meetings or meetings in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you were close to Minister Boskoski, you never saw Minister Boskoski with Johan Tarculovski, in the company of Johan Tarculovski, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I never did see him in the company of Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see Johan Tarculovski at any given time enter the cabinet of the minister or the director of public security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have never seen him in these two offices. In the ministry, I don't know. Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally know -- knew Johan Tarculovski as a person, a member of the personal security team of the president of the Republic, or rather, the wife of the president of the Republic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that the head of the security of the president of the Republic at that time was Zlatko Kitkovski [phoen]. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Zlatko Kitkovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore you had direct cooperation and communication with Zlatko Kitkovski, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this happened at times when the president would ask for the minister or when the minister had to call in to the president. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes. Our practice was that the -- one of the person who took care of his security had the mobile phone, had his mobile phone so when the president or the prime minister called, the minister would speak with these persons. Oftentimes, Kitkovski Zlatko, yes, requested the minister when the president had done so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That would in fact be my next question to you. It was the usual practice that the minister, or the president, or the prime minister, not have their mobile phones on their persons but that they be with their security, and through the security the other security will be contacted or directly the president or the minister. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, this was not only the practice in the case of Minister Boskoski but this was practice, the practice also among other important persons which were protected.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it worked most of the time with most persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you said that for the most part the minister gave the orders or you had consultations with him about the jobs which you were to carry out, did it ever happen that the person who was being protected sometimes asked of his body-guards to do something without having consulted you on it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a rule in your security at that time that if a body-guard received such an order from the minister, that this order is carried out but that you are informed about the job which he has conducted at the personal order of the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your communication with the colleagues from other security teams, did you know that the president of the Republic often issued direct orders to the body-guards sometimes contrary to those which they received from the head of security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you are aware that the president of the Republic often issued certain orders to the ministries also, not only to his security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the security of the president included persons who he personally requested to be in his security team which was somewhat unusual for the way -- in terms of the way you selected your team of security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it was unusual. He -- in one period of time he requested that his team be increased with people from the Ministry of the Defence and one of his close relatives from his immediate family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly what I wanted to say. Is it true that on the basis of his personal order most of the members of -- from the army joined the security team of the president of the Republic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that in this time it was well known that President Trajkovski, because of an assassination attempt while he was in parliament that he had substantial fear, that he was afraid that he would be killed and that he always requested an increase in his security and he requested people which had his confidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he felt insecure and he was constantly requesting an increase in his security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very important persons, especially the president of the Republic had the right to protection of members of their families. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Minister Boskoski did not have special protection for his family because you were small in number but nonetheless you managed to secure in general his house in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of a small period of time when his family was in Croatia, then we had certain information that his family was in danger that in certain restaurants and pastry shops people were meeting who wanted to cause harm to his family and this information came to the Ministry of Interior in Skopje, and as far as can I recall, the colleague with whom I communicated with and later on saw him, this was in August 2001, Zoran was his name, Adriancic, I think was his last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, there was a real reason due to which you, at the end of July, or I don't know the precise date, went to the Republic of Croatia and stayed there about 20 days so as -- to agree with your colleagues from the security, from Croatia to agree upon the manner of-- on which -- of how the ministers' wives would be protected?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Because our competencies ended with the borders of the Republic of Macedonia. We met with persons from the Ministry of Interior of Croatia and we agreed that the security or, rather, to place security over the family of and the premises where the family of Ljube Boskoski lived and this is how it happened. 24-hour watch, security, from our Croatian colleagues. I think three to four each day, per day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just as you acted in this position, so the president of the Republic had the right to have regular protection of his wife and family. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia and a police officer, you were aware that the president of the Republic, in accordance the constitution was the commander in chief, and that during the time of the crisis he often issues orders. Are aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague asked you about going visits to such places of crisis. First I would ask you something directly in correlation with your tasks and duties. We saw on the video-clip that was shown to you that the minister was in military uniform and that most persons wore protective equipment. When you went to the areas where you knew -- where you knew there were fighting in the vicinity, did you place special requests before the minister so as to ensure his security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We asked that he carry and wear protective equipment, which -- which includes bullet-proof vests and uniform, camouflage uniform, boots and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This request, as head of security, was linked with his personal security, not about his place and role in the area where he was going. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you went to these areas, which was individually listed to you by my colleague, Ratae, Vaksince, Tetovo, Matejce and so forth, when you went to these areas where the joint operations were carried out of the army and the police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you at that time hear the president of the Republic clearly say in public his position about the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia and that he deems the NLA as a terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He always considered NLA as a terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you hear that he often qualified the activities of the NLA as criminal and illegal activities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He emphasised this, and -- whereby he always said that the damage is equally distributed among the Macedonians and the Albanians who live in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During these public addresses is it true that he said that these terrorist groups should be expelled from the territory of the Republic of Macedonia and that peace for all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, Albanians and Macedonians, should be returned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your position as head of security, you probably did not have insight into his written orders but what you're testifying now is what you could have heard, either directly from the president, or from his public addresses. Is -- is my understanding of this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you stated a while ago that the president often issued orders so often to the minister, has it happened that you were present somewhere in a car, in the house, or elsewhere, and were able to hear the president issuing a direct order to the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it happened quite often. During the crisis period I remember that usually minister, not often, made comments when he entered the car that he had received an order that maybe he disagreed with, but I didn't want to go into this and I think that one of such orders was when the Lions needed to secure the exhumation of the Macedonians who disappeared in the conflict of 2001. That was at Neprosteno locality where the exhumation needed to take place and during this action, as far as I remember, that was the first action where the Lions were involved and during that action three police officers were killed at Trebos and then the minister said when he entered the car that he had received an order from the president to secure the space, the area in and around Neprosteno and the road to Neprosteno in order to perform the exhumation of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you have already mentioned that exhumation at Neprosteno, could I then refresh your memory that was in the second or towards mid-November 2001 and is it correct that that was the first action where the Lions participated and where they had significant losses?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. It was winter, there was snow. I think it was somewhere towards the middle or the end of November, don't take my word for it, and three police officers of the Ministry of Interior were killed, members of the Rapid Intervention Unit, Lions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you had just stated that exhumation was ordered by the president of the Republic directly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't seen that decision but immediately after the meeting of the minister of the interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski, and the late president Boris Trajkovski, when the minister entered the car he stated that he needed to send the units immediately to the Tetovo area, to Neprosteno, in order to secure the exhumation. That was an order coming from the President Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would this be the time for the break or should we continue, since we started a bit later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Shall we continue for somewhere between five and ten minutes, as is convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once we started speaking about the orders of the president, you, when asked by my learned colleague, you were explaining the political responsibility and indicated that the minister, after the events in Skopje on the 25th of June, offered his resignation to the president of the government. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after these events of 25th of June, 2001, where several thousands of citizens participated, part of the reserve forces of the police and of the army, the minister made the decision to disband the reserve forces. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It was the same decision -- that same decision, as far as I remember, was revoked by the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You answered the question that I haven't asked you, so that decision of the minister about the disbandment was annulled by the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I just don't recall whether it was done on the same day or the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to this situation, the exhumation in Neprosteno that you spoke about towards the middle or the end of November 2001, is it correct that there was enormous pressure on the president of the Republic by the families of the disappeared persons and also politicians from the local communities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The opposition parties and the families of the persons who have disappeared, there were also threats of hunger strike and other things. There was a lot of pressure on the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And was the president known to say that he made many decisions under the pressure of the victims and the politicians maybe from Tetovo or some of the other local communities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But regardless of the way in which the president made the decision, was your understanding that the minister had the duty to enforce the order and then others needed to enforce the orders of the president?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The president emphasised this often that he was the commander in chief and that his were the last words.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated a while ago, when they went to the exhumation at Neprosteno, at Trebos there was an ambush by the terrorist groups and three police officers were killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, let's go back to the questions asked by my learned colleague the Prosecutor and that are related to Ljuboten. You said that you were outside of Macedonia on the 12th of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in general, whether you were in communication with your deputy who remained in Macedonia during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke on the phone. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we said the name of your deputy or substitute but could you repeat what was the name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that was my colleague Branko Pejcinovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that date, or the next day, the 12th or 13th of August, 2001, did you speak on the phone with Branko Pejcinovski and did you receive any information from him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that he and the minister went to the barbers. The president called on the phone, actually first his head of security requested to speak with the minister and that he sent them to certain area to go and see what was happening there. I think that my colleague phoned me before they left Ljuboten and he told me then that they went to an unknown area. They were taken there by a police officer from the Mirkovci police station where they had the first meeting. He was an ethnic Albanian. I think that was some head of a sector or a person in charge of admission of persons at that police station. So a commanding officer. They went to the scene. I don't think how long they remained there and he just said that was when they were returning that they went with a passenger car wearing shirts, suits so they were inadequately protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So from the conversation with your deputy, you could understand that when he received the order from the president, the minister actually didn't know what was taking place at that area, where he needed to go. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes. We saw in the video-clip when we had information that there was exchange of fire somewhere, we requested the minister to wear appropriate clothes, so the very fact that the minister went there wearing a suit and the security wearing casual clothes without protective clothes, without arms, just their personal armament and not formation armament in a passenger car and not with a bullet-proof car, this is self-evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just a few more question on another topic with the witness, so maybe this would be the convenient time to break, and then I will finish within the next ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at ten past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, you stated a while ago that the Minister Boskoski is a very rich man because he has many friends. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that Minister Boskoski has many friends, among them ethnic Macedonians and ethnic Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Minister Boskoski was born in a village where the Albanians and the Macedonians used to live together and they still live together. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he grew up with the Albanians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the head of his personal security, you know that during the crisis he was in constant communication with the Albanian population. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the crisis, he also went to the Albanian villages, he went into their homes and he spoke to them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the crisis and after that, until the elections, his deputy in the Ministry of Interior was an ethnic Albanian, Refet Almazi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, as a close associate of the Minister Boskoski are aware that Minister Boskoski was not only a friend in terms of working relations with Mr. Elmazi but also before the crisis, throughout the crisis and after the crisis they had also personal friendship?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know that, together with Mr. Elmazi, Minister Boskoski worked intensively on the recruitment of Albanians for the police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you became head of the personal security of the minister, you probably heard that Minister Boskoski and Refet Elmazi tried to introduce mixed police stations even before he became a minister.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, when he was a state secretary. An example of this could be the police station at Brest or Gosince. Then the minister went -- he was a state secretary then together with the deputy minister Refet Elmazi to launch, to open the police station and to distribute humanitarian assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned Brest, I will remind you that this could have been towards the middle of March 2001, and, as you just stated, the deputy minister Refet Elmazi and Mr. Boskoski went up there to establish the mixed police station. So the police station where Macedonians and Albanians would work on an equal footing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, they brought significant humanitarian assistance for the Albanian villages that were cut off for a long time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also know that the terrorist groups of the NLA then attacked both deputy minister Elmazi and the Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A police officer was killed in that event and the introduction of rights for the Albanian population was prevented. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You learned the information about this event mainly from the minister because he often would say that the Albanian terrorists are working against their own people, quoting the example of Brest precisely. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that the minister spoke fiercely against the terrorist groups and the gangs but he always made an absolute distinction between those terrorists and the Albanian population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He always -- often said in the public but I would say also in personal communications and if that is correct please confirm this.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, what did I say? He spoke about that in the public; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He spoke publicly that the Albanians in Macedonia were under the pressure of the terrorists, as the Macedonians were. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, are you aware that in August 2001 or towards the end of August 2001, the terrorists attacked the restaurant Brioni not far from the native village of Minister Boskoski, Celopek, where two of his neighbours were killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go and visit Celopek then with the Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we visited Celopek. We had problems during our visit, not in the sense that somebody tried to stone us or -- or spoke insults against the minister and the vehicles that went in his company, but we had problems in the sense that many people wanted to greet him, shake hands of him so we needed to go out of the protocol to go back. We visited some fields owned by the minister. He spoke to the local population. It was just Albanians then and the group that escorted the minister, the body-guards and then we continued our trip to Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment that we spoke with the Albanians do you remember that he said then that the Macedonians should not respond to such terrorist attacks through retaliation against the Albanian population and he said that the Albanians must -- that the Macedonians must do everything to maintain their good neighbourly relations with their Albanian neighbours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But he then also said, as he always has stated, that there must be an energetic response in doing away with the terrorist groups that terrorise both the Macedonian and the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated, he also met with the Albanians in the village but that was not the only encounter with the Albanians. The minister frequently went to other areas and he would meet with the Albanian population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. Let's take the example of the fact that throughout the conflict the house in Celopek where the Albanian population are a majority, the house of the minister, of his parents was not attacked, throughout the war, throughout the military conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, Mr. Trajkovski, if I say to you that the Minister Boskoski expressed his attitude towards the Albanian population very frequently in the following way and I will now present the position how would the minister express this position of his, so he would say: "Nobody should ask me to change my upbringing that I received at my home to have love for all people regardless of their ethnic, national or religious background and I really love them, especially those who love Macedonia or at least respect Macedonia and the Macedonians. "I grew up together with the Albanians. With them in my native Celopek, I have spent the best years of my boyhood and adulthood. We had very simple -- we simply had friendship and we played together. We sometimes fought, of course, in the way kids do, and sometimes there would be fights at the meadow in -- instead of fighting, we would be wrestling and I was known to win, but there were many times that I was won over. I was always well perceived and well received at the homes of the Albanians and they were at our homes and at the homes of other Macedonians." Would this that I read now be the way in which Ljube Boskoski responding to frequent questions in the public would speak about his attitude towards the Albanians in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree with what you stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, I quoted from the book, My Fight for Macedonia. That is Exhibit P -- I don't see the number now precisely, but I will state the number later. That is Prosecutor's Exhibit's P something, but I don't know the number at the moment and I apologise for not having it prepared in advance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The quote I just read is what you have heard personally from the minister on many occasions in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we have heard it and we felt it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the book My Fight For Macedonia is P402.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the minister received letters from Macedonians but also from the Albanians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that he once received a letter from a young Albanian girl who wrote to him because she wanted to fight alongside the Macedonian police officers and defend Macedonia because her parents were born in Macedonia and she herself was born in Macedonia. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Minister Boskoski held on to this letter with great pride for a long time, the letter of this young Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Allow me just the following question. After the elections in 2002, the new power were -- was established at the end of 2002. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that then the minister told you that -- that the Bucoski government, the government of Bucoski, that the -- that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, is it true that the minister then told you that Vlado Bucoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- former minister of the defence of the Republic of Macedonia gave him a document of the army of the Republic of Macedonia from which it derived that the order for the entry of the forces in Ljuboten was issued by President Trajkovski. Did you have such a conversation with the minister.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this conversation, just as you said. It is correct. I verify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this report he gave to Goran Mitevski who then gave it to the new Minister of the Interior Hari Kostov?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you only heard this from the minister, is it your deep conviction that this is correct in view of the fact that for two years you knew the way in which the president of the Republic issued orders and how he sometimes -- he himself asked of -- that something be done notwithstanding his ministers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished with my questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tarculovski -- Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Acting according to the guidelines of the Chamber, the Defence, together with that of Ljube Boskoski, we have coordinated our position on this witness. Therefore, I will not be asking this witness any additional questions and I stand in support of the questioning carried out by my colleague Edina Residovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovski, today on page 34 of the transcript you had said that the important person which is being secured determines the jobs and tasks you should be carrying out. Were these the jobs and tasks that were related to the important person's security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not often.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, I guess, is: These tasks and jobs that you were given from the protected person, what did they entail?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question or rephrase the question? I do not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, I'm a little confused; I apologise. You were given tasks and jobs from the protected person. I'm just wondering on a daily basis what those tasks or jobs might have been.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: According to me, an order is when the minister of interior calls and tells me that we have to be at his place at 9.00. An order is when he tells his secretary at 9.00 or 10.00 the security should be at his place. An order is when he tells his secretary to call persons to a collegium, regardless whether it be general this or director that or so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So the orders that you received from Minister Boskoski at that time whether related to you carrying out the duties with respect to his security.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is what I said. Most frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 40 of today's transcript you were also asked about the collegiums that we went over in your statement. Can I ask you, did the collegiums occur to your recollection in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. On page 45 of today's transcript you also indicated that you never heard Mr. Boskoski, as a minister, issuing orders. And I believe you also referenced this on page 16 and you stated that Mr. Boskoski did not issue orders in your presence when you both visited the units in the field. As the minister of the interior, though, he did issue orders. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just a second ago you told me that he would -- and you gave examples of orders by the Ministry of Interior that he would order -- order you to be at his place at 9.00 or he would order his secretary to have the security ordered to be at his place. So I'm asking you, as a minister of the interior, did Mr. Boskoski issue orders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: If you mean about this which you are just saying, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked -- you were actually asked about an incident at Neprosteno in the Tetovo area about exhumations there and this is on page 58 of today's transcript. You testified that in response to the president's orders, Mr. Boskoski then ordered units to go to the Tetovo area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- you testified about the conversation that Minister Boskoski related to you about an order that he received from the president regarding the exhumations in Neprosteno. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He did not tell this to me. He just made comments on it I presume with someone either on the phone or something. I cannot recall precisely, but I understood when he was entering into the vehicle that he was commenting an order given by the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you indicated on page 59, actually, of today's transcript that when the minister entered the car, he stated that he had needed to send the units immediately to the Tetovo area. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With respect to the reports that were filed by persons in the security sector, you stated on page 50 of today's transcript that you did not -- actually, you and persons in the security sector, did not submit reports to the assistant minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps once maybe, when the vehicle was attacked and the vehicle of the minister was damaged in front of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Because we believed that this is part of his work and that he has to be informed of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you mean "part of his," meaning the assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That is what I asked. So if something happened during your duty which would cause you to file a report - I know you're telling us you only filed one before - but if something happened which would cause you to file a report, that report would then be submitted to the protected person, that is the person you were protecting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know what to answer to this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood. You said the protected person. I thought you said the assistant minister. Yes, if you mean about the protected person, the minister, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand you correctly, if something happened that caused you to file a report during your duty, that report then would be filed only with the Minister Boskoski at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: There was no such case but usually the minister should be informed and also the assistant minister for security.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. So there was some method of informing the assistant minister as well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is how things should have gone. Up until now this has not happened with the exception of this one case I mentioned which transpired in front of the building of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If the Ministry of Interior itself needed additional staff could they pool staff from your security sector?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If the Ministry of Interior in 2001 needed additional staff, could they pool persons from the security staff, the security sector?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 69 of today's transcript you indicated that you had received information about a report given to Goran Mitevski. You never actually saw this report, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, I have not seen the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And going back to page 58 of today's transcript where you testified about exhumations in Neprosteno, can I ask you has anyone spoken to you about the evidence you're providing today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAJKOVSKI
utterances.text: That someone spoke to me about what I'm saying now? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you then. You will be pleased to know that concludes the questions for you. You will be free to return to your normal activities. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you've given. And the court officer will show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It has been a pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, I take it that concludes the evidence available today, so we will adjourn then to resume at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
